key_insight: Ocean surface wave spectra in fully developed seas are better represented by a k^-2.5 (ω^-4) tail than the commonly used k^-3 (ω^-5) form, especially when peak wavenumber, significant wave height, and wind speed are known.
engineering_relevance: Using an updated spectrum parameterization can materially change predicted air-sea roughness and Marine Atmospheric Boundary Layer behavior, affecting coastal, naval, and climate-related engineering models.
method: Compared two widely used wave-spectrum parameterizations against field data
Tested fetch-limited, fully developed, and mixed sea conditions
Used LES of Marine Atmospheric Boundary Layers to assess roughness sensitivity
evidence_signal: Field campaign observations and LES comparisons show the alternative fully developed-sea parameterization better matches measured spectra and can produce significantly different equivalent roughness estimates.
watch_item: The improved tail form is condition-dependent, so applying it outside fully developed or well-characterized sea states may reduce accuracy.
paper_title: Observations and empirical functions for the ocean surface wave spectrum
